column1: # W46 detector-parity, EXTENDED to the strongest published baselines.
# WHY. The existing parity control (logs/xds8b_abl2 + w46_parity alpha sweep)
# only grafts the OmniParser prior onto DivPrune and VisPruner, whose unpruned
# ScreenSpot-v2 scores at rho=10% are 51.97 / 51.73. PruneSID reaches 58.96 and
# CDPruner is the other instruction-conditioned selector, so a control that
# skips exactly the two strongest arms reads as cherry-picked: "you only helped
# the baselines that could not catch you anyway". This TSV closes that hole.
# HOW the prior enters each selector's OWN score channel (no new mechanism, and
# never a second stage bolted on top):
#   cdpruner  -- DPP relevance r~ <- r~ * m, renormalised to max 1 so the
#                relevance/diversity balance keeps its published scale.
#   prunesid  -- PCA loading magnitudes <- loading * m, so a detected token wins
#                intra-group NMS ties and quota slots; grouping, adaptive
#                threshold and quota arithmetic untouched.
# Unit-tested in scripts/_w46_test_hybrid_ext.py: constant mass (= what an empty
# detection yields) reproduces the published keep set bit-exactly, peaked mass
# pulls the keep set toward the detected block, budget is conserved, and a
# non-hybrid selector fails loud.
# Two prior strengths per cell for the same reason as w46_parity_alpha.tsv: the
# baseline mass is m = 1 + alpha*P with P in [0,1], while TRACE's BAM mass is
# m = 1 + alpha*n*p with p a probability measure, so equal alpha under-powers the
# baseline by ~n. Reporting each parity arm at its own best alpha is the reading
# least favourable to us.
# BENCHMARK|TASK|TRACK|EXP_ARM|RATIO|HIST_N|OUT|LIMIT|EXTRA_ENV
